explanation: Shoes are left in the genkan, a lower entrance area. Many homes keep a separate pair of slippers just for the toilet, and tatami rooms are entered barefoot or in socks.

claims.text: In Japanese homes, guests who remove their shoes are usually offered slippers.
Guests are not usually offered socks, wooden clogs or straw sandals; geta and zori are outdoor footwear.
Shoes are left in the genkan, the lower entrance area of a Japanese home.
Many Japanese homes keep separate slippers for the toilet.
Slippers are taken off before stepping onto tatami mats.
